prose: The engine is headless. It runs under plain Node with no bundler, so a DOM reference typechecks clean under a shared config and then dies at runtime in the CLI.
rationale: This is why the tsconfigs are split; the invariant is the runtime half of that guarantee.

prose: The renderer reaches the Electron main process only through the preload bridge, never by importing it.
rationale: Renderer code displays agent-authored text and is treated as untrusted; a direct import would put main-process capability in its bundle.

prose: The engine is the product and the app is one consumer of it, so nothing in engine/ may reach into app/.
rationale: It has to keep running standalone as a CLI with no Electron and no React present.

prose: Unevidenced claims are rejected where they are ingested, not at review time. The guard lives in the claim store.
rationale: This is the single defence against a confabulated map; if it moves or disappears the whole design's honesty claim goes with it.

prose: The harness never passes an adapter flag that bypasses approvals or sandboxing.
rationale: Agents observe and claim; they never write code. A bypass flag would silently remove the only thing keeping that true.

prose: Nothing under engine/scene/ calls a randomness source. Position is a pure function of the focus stack, so the same repo lays out the same way every session — which is the only thing that makes flying around build spatial memory.
